correctness.rationale: For D_n with strictly increasing 0<a1<...<an and normalized height average, the trapezoidal vertex formula gives coordinates sigma_j(t_{j+1}-t_{j-1})/(4A) and -(t1+tk)/(4A) in the nth direction. For one intermediate point, squared norm is [1+(t/A)^2]/4, attaining maximum exactly at ±e_{n-1}. For k>=2 the squared norm is convex on -B<=t1<=...<=tk<=B; independently enumerated its ordered-simplex vertices for rational A>B and k=2..9 and checked the proof’s extremal forms, max Fk<=2(A+B)^2. Thus clearance >=(A-B)^2/(8A^2) and no multi-point path contacts. The antipodal extremal pair forces the minimum-radius centered origin ball, uniqueness by squared-distance averaging, and unique diametral pair; no affine-coordinate metric changes are assumed. Coherent-path enumeration relies on the genuinely applicable Black-De Loera indexing theorem; finite exact tests corroborate but are not all-real proof.
